the correlation between the VHI and some acoustic parameters in patients with MTD.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VHI is a valid and reliable instrument in assessing the impact of MTD on the patient's quality of life.
VHI is not interchangeable with acoustic measures but the correlation between V HI and some acoustic parameters increases in the same type of dysphonia.
the correlation between V HI and some laboratory measurements increase in dysphonia with the same origin, the same nature, the same sex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a correlation between VHI with some specific acoustic measures, but it does not mean that the VHI is a good predictor of the acoustic measures.
the VHI and acoustic measures of speech are not interchangeable.
the correlation between the acoustic parameters and VHI is not strong enough to use them interchangeably.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VHI is a subjective tool that can be used to assess patients with MTD, and the acoustic parameters are objective tools that can be used as complementary tools for assessing patients with MTD.
the voice handicap index is a good measure of the impact of dysphonia on the life of patients with muscle tension dysphonia.
the correlation between VVI and some laboratory measurements increase in dysphonia with the same nature, the same origin and the same sexuality.
